1. Purpose. The Navy Reserve provides drilling opportunities to those Sailors living Outside
the Continental United States (OCONUS). This article addresses the unique issues and policies
regarding Selected Reservists (SELRES) and Voluntary Training Unit (VTU) Sailors living
OCONUS and for units with an OCONUS drill site.
2. Application.
a. This article applies to non-command billet application and assignment procedures for
SELRES junior Officers and enlisted personnel living overseas.
b. For senior officers residing overseas, refer to the current Commander, Navy Reserve
Force Notice 5400 and Navy Administrative message for command billet application and
assignment procedures/policies via the APPLY process.
c. Overseas VTU Sailors will be assigned to overseas'VTU units. VTU assignments and
associated polices are addressed in reference (a).
3. Defmitions.
a. Overseas residences. Are defined in references (b) and ( c ). For purposes of this article;
Alaska, Hawaii, Puerto Rico, and Guam are not considered OCONUS, due to the presence of
Navy Reserve Activities at these locations.

b. Overseas reserve units. Are those that execute drills at overseas locations and are
attached to Navy Reserve Center (NRC) Guam or Navy Reserve Center Jacksonville for
administrative support.
c. Continental United States (CONUS) reserve units. For the purpose of this instruction are
reserve units that execute drills in CONUS, Alaska, Hawaii, Puerto Rico, or Guam.
d. Drilling Reservist. For the purpose of this instruction include SELRES and VTU
members.
4. NRC Supporting Overseas Reserve Units Areas of Responsibilities.
a. NRC Guam is the supporting NRC for drilling reservists in the Pacific Command AOR.
b. NRC Jacksonville is the supporting NRC for drilling reservists in the European,
Southern, Central, and Africa Command AORs.
c. Specific overseas units by NRC:

d. NRC Tampa is the supporting NRC for Overseas drilling reservists assigned to Special
Operations Command.
5. Responsibilities.
a. Commander, Navy Reserve Forces Command N12 will assign Drilling Reservists with
overseas residences to Overseas Reserve Units.
b. Reserve Program Directors (RPD):
(1) May authorized individual OCONUS inactive duty training (IDT) locations at
supported commands in accordance with location's Status of Force Agreement (SOFA). The
supported command must accept responsibility for:
(a) E-muster of Sailor's IDT/drill participation.

(b) Coordination of Semi-Annual Physical Fitness Assessment (PF A).
(c) Notification and documentation of any deficiencies in Sailor's conduct forwarded
to reserve unit CO.
( d) Establishment of a .mil or .gov email as necessary.
(e) Coordination of Medical and Dental readiness support.
(f) Coordination of administrative requirements to include Career Development
Boards for enlisted personnel as necessary.
(g) Logistical support to enable Sailors to execute additional administrative or
training requirements as appropriate.
(2) Will coordinate with local Judge Advocate General Corp (JAG) to ensure adherence
to specific country SOFA and reference ( d), prior to establishment of OCONUS units and/or drill
sites.
(3) May submit Exception to Policy to COMNA VRESFORCOM Nl2 for OCONUS
members desiring CONUS billets.
c. Navy Reserve Activity (NRA) will notify COMNA VRESFOR Nl2 of Sailor's change of
residence and ensure NSIPS is updated.
d. Unit COs/OICs and RPDs must properly identify applicable overseas information in the
billet description to include requirements, IDT location, and drill site specifics.
e. Sailors transitioning to an overseas residence must:
(1) Update their new home address in Navy Standard Integrated Personnel System
(NSIPS). Overseas Sailors must include the country in which they reside to facilitate proper
assignments. Sailors must enter their actual street address in the, "foreign" locality screen in
addition to updating their Army Post Office (APO) or Fleet Post Office (FPO) address in the
APO or FPO· locality screens, respectively.
(2) Notify Nl2 via NRA to request reassignment to OCONUS unit.
(3) Reference (e) restricts funding for Sailors to travel from locations outside the US to
the US for inactive duty training travel (IDTT), active duty for training, and annual training (AT)
orders. Overseas Sailors desiring to drill at CONUS locations shall route ETP requests via RPD
and will be responsible for all travel expenses to drilling site.

( 4) Will apply for advertised billets in overseas reserve units. Application for these
billets indicates that the Sailors accept personal responsibility to travel for all costs incurred in
traveling to the unit's respective drill site.
f. Overseas Drilling Reservists must:
(1) Maintain Minimum Satisfactory Participation Requirements per RESPERSMAN
1001-010 and drill at the designated overseas location or locally at the NRA.
(2) Comply with Department of State travel advisories and the Department of Defense
Foreign Clearance Guide and must comply with applicable clearance requirements.
(3) Update address in NSIPS as applicable.
(4) Sailors who are residing outside the US must include the location when requesting to
Telework per reference (f} for drill to ensure NR Unit Commanding Officer can assess internet
security. Members residing in specific countries may be barred from being in a duty status while
in that country by SOFA. Sailors and COs will reference the Foreign Clearance Guidance for
prior to submitting or approving telework applications.
6. IDT and AT Obligation;
a. IDT Obligation.
(1) Reference RESPERSMAN 1570-010 for IDT Participation Requirements.
(2) Per references (b) and (g), RPDs may not authorize any funded IDTT orders for
Sailors residing overseas.
(3) Per reference (d), IDT is not authorized in imminent danger areas, which are listed in
reference (g).
b. AT Obligation.
( 1) Reference RESPERSMAN 1571-010 for information concerning AT/ ADT
requirements.
(2) Sailors residing OCONUS may not perform AT/ADT in the United States if travel
costs are involved without prior approval from COMNAVRESFORCOM (N33). RPDs may
submit policy exceptions to COMNA VRESFORCOM (N33) on a case by-case basis per
reference (c).
